questions.stem: Why does earthing a fuel tanker prevent explosions?

options.text: It provides a conducting path for charge to flow safely to the ground
It increases the charge on the tanker
It removes all the fuel vapour from the air

questions.explanation: Earthing provides a conducting path that allows any static charge that builds up on the tanker to flow safely to the ground. This prevents dangerous charge accumulation that could otherwise produce a spark and ignite fuel vapour.

questions.stem: In an electrostatic precipitator, how are smoke particles removed from the air?

options.text: Smoke is filtered through a fine mesh
Smoke particles are cooled until they condense
Smoke particles are charged and then attracted to oppositely charged collecting plates
Smoke particles are dissolved in water

questions.explanation: In an electrostatic precipitator, smoke passes through a charged metal grid which charges the particles. These charged particles are then attracted to oppositely charged collecting plates where they stick, allowing clean air to exit the chimney.
